title: Python 3.12.14, 3.11.16, and 3.10.21 Security Releases Now Available
summary: The Python development team has released security updates for Python 3.12, 3.11, and 3.10. These releases address multiple critical vulnerabilities, including path traversal, HTTP header injection, XML parsing crashes, denial-of-service risks, and memory corruption issues. Key fixes involve modules like `tarfile`, `webbrowser`, `ftplib`, `http.cookies`, `xml.parsers.expat`, and `shutil`. Users are strongly encouraged to upgrade to mitigate security risks.
key_points: Fixes for **15+ CVEs**, including path traversal in `tarfile`, HTTP header injection in `wsgiref`, and XML parsing crashes in `xml.parsers.expat`.
`webbrowser.open()` now rejects URLs with leading dashes to prevent command injection.
`ftplib` no longer trusts IPv4 addresses from PASV commands by default (CVE-2021-4189 mitigation).
`shutil.unpack_archive()` skips ZIP files with Windows drive prefixes to prevent arbitrary file writes.
Memory corruption fixes in `lzma`, `bz2`, and `zlib` decompressors.
Updated bundled `libexpat` to version 2.8.3 for improved XML security.
ConfigParser and TOML parsing hardened against crafted inputs causing excessive CPU usage.
Highly recommended for all users of affected versions to upgrade immediately.
